speaker: Arne Slot
quote_text:
Tough day for you out there. What are your  thoughts on the game and the result? The result is  
obvious. That's a big disappointment. And the way  we played wasn't a lot to be happy about as well.  
The only thing I was happy about is that the boys  kept on fighting for 100 minutes and probably the  
best part of our game were the last 10 minutes.  So that tells you that they kept on fighting, but  
credits to them. Good game plan. Worked incredibly  hard and got a penalty that was rewarded,  
deserved, because it was a penalty, clear penalty,  correct decision. But that had a lot of impact on  
the game, of course, because both teams hardly had  any chance and all of a sudden you get a penalty  
kick. Again, which was the correct decision, but  that, and then they were one all up and they kept  
on fighting till the end, and goalkeeper made one  or two good saves in the end, but yeah, we hardly  
created anything at all. John, I appreciate you've  got lots of games and fixtures at the moment,  
but anything great about the team, the line-up  and the players that you're feeling today? No,  
because you never know what would have happened if  we would have played with our starters over here.  
I think during this season we've seen a few times  already that it's a game plan, a playing style  
which is difficult for our starters, but also for  the ones that have played today. So constantly,  
loan balls, second balls, loan balls, second balls  is difficult for every team. We had this with  
United at home, for example, as well. They had a  similar playing style, going to a very low bar,  
kick every ball long. And then we played with our  starters. So I think today also showed why we play  
with the ones that we've played today, because  these players need game rhythm as well. And for  
them to be ready in the upcoming months, they  need the game time. And you saw today that some  
of these players really need games like this to be  ready for the last three months of the season. For  
the pressure that you had at the end, you must  have felt as if you'd get a breakthrough. Yeah,  
yeah, there were one or two big chances, but I  think if a team is working so hard and throws  
themselves for every ball there on a certain  kind of momentum, and then maybe you deserve  
to be a bit lucky as well in the end, and then  the goalkeeper made one or two great saves,  
but this is what you see a lot. If they would have  played 10 to 15% less or work 10 to 15% less, you  
probably would have scored it. But you see many  times that if a team brings such a performance in,  
yeah, you saw yesterday, was it with City  that they missed a big chance in the end,  
the other team? So sometimes you deserve a bit  of luck if you work as hard as Plymouth did  
today. I'm looking to do basketball, Joe Gomez.  Yeah. Is it the same injury that brought him off  
against my stand a few weeks back or? I'm not too  sure. I'm not too sure if it was the same leg, but  
I haven't had time to ask him. But it was clear  that I think we all know which moment he felt a  
bit insecure about because he didn't sprint back  fully. And then he said, yeah, I'm not 100% sure.  
I'm afraid if I make one extra sprint, that things  will go wrong. So I don't know exactly where he  
is. It didn't, it didn't, it's not, how do you  say this? It's not, sorry. Torn. It's not torn,  
I assume. But it didn't feel good for him. And  that was a bit of a blow because Curtis Jones  
was on the bench, but he came to me this morning  and said, I don't think I'm fully recovered yet  
as well. after the training session of yesterday  and that all of a sudden led to the fact that we  
were with a few more youngsters on the pitch than  was the idea before the game. But still there was  
enough quality on the pitch to get a better result  than this. The players that you left back at home,  
what were their schedule? They trained  yesterday and they will train tomorrow  
again. I think that'll do them well. Is that what  they needed? Yeah, yeah, most of the things we do,  
we do for a reason. So we just don't do all of  a sudden something. I said before that we have  
to play many games now. The Aston Villa game  comes during the week again as well. So the  
last few weeks, we've played every single week two  times. The upcoming weeks, we have to play every  
single time two games. And And therefore, it's  not only for them good to once in a while have  
a week where they only play one game, but also  for the ones that were here today, they need need  
the intensity of the game because you can keep on  training with them, but once in a while they need  
a game as well, and they had that against PSV.  Unfortunately, we lost that one, and they had  
that today, and unfortunately, we lost this one  again as well. Isaac, he came on, and then you  
took him off. You had the word with him. What did  you say to him, Arthur? I think it's a fantastic  
moment for every player to make a debut for him  as well. But I felt I had to take him off for two  
reasons. He was already on a yellow and it was a  game with a lot of duels, with a lot of intensity  
and that's their playing style and they bring a  lot of long balls in. So if you're one time wrong,  
it's a yellow again. And it was a game that was  hard enough with 11, let alone with 10. And I felt  
we needed to make an offensive substitution. And  the other three were Durrell. Wata and Costas and  
it didn't seem smart to me to take one of these  three off. So yeah, that to that decision and  
I thought I had to tell him because yeah, making  your debut and then be taken off after an hour or  
something like that is very disappointing for him,  of course. Have a good trip. Thank you. Take care.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Plymouth Argyle 1-0 Liverpool
